toc.label: Structural Intervention Distance (SID)
toc.definition: A graph-based pre-metric counting ordered node pairs for which two DAGs disagree on the parent-adjustment set, i.e. would predict different interventional distributions.
sub_questions: Why is edge-counting (SHD) a poor proxy for causal error?

toc.label: Causal DAG
toc.definition: A directed acyclic graph whose edges encode direct causal influences and whose structure licenses do-interventions.
sub_questions: What does a directed edge mean causally?

toc.label: Intervention Distribution
toc.definition: The distribution of the outcome after forcing a variable to a value via do(X=x), computed by the truncated-factorization / parent-adjustment formula.
sub_questions: How does do(X=x) differ from conditioning on X=x?

toc.label: Parent Adjustment
toc.definition: Estimating a causal effect by adjusting for the intervened node's parents in the assumed DAG.
sub_questions: Why are the parents a valid adjustment set?

toc.label: Structural Hamming Distance (SHD)
toc.definition: A baseline graph distance that counts how many edges differ between two (partially) directed graphs.
sub_questions: What causal mistakes does SHD fail to see?

toc.label: Graphical Formulation of SID
toc.definition: An equivalent definition of SID using only graphical adjustment criteria, avoiding any density computation.
sub_questions: Which adjustment criterion replaces the distributions?

toc.label: Valid Adjustment Set
toc.definition: A node set whose adjustment yields the correct interventional distribution; SID checks whether the estimate's parent set is valid in the true DAG.
sub_questions: When is an adjustment set valid?

toc.label: Metric Properties of SID
toc.definition: SID is a pre-metric: non-negative and zero on identical graphs, but asymmetric and not satisfying the triangle inequality in general.
sub_questions: Why only a pre-metric and not a metric?

toc.label: CPDAG
toc.definition: A completed partially directed acyclic graph representing a Markov equivalence class, the typical output of methods like the PC algorithm.
sub_questions: Why do causal discovery methods return a CPDAG, not a DAG?

toc.label: SID for CPDAG Estimates
toc.definition: Lower and upper SID bounds when the estimate is a Markov equivalence class rather than a single DAG.
sub_questions: How is an interval of SID values defined over an equivalence class?

toc.label: Symmetrized SID
toc.definition: A symmetric variant summing SID in both directions, for comparing two DAGs neither of which is an estimate of the other.
sub_questions: When is symmetry the right choice?

toc.label: SID versus SHD (Simulation)
toc.definition: Random-DAG experiments showing SID and SHD rank graph errors differently.
sub_questions: Where do SID and SHD most disagree?

toc.label: Comparing Causal Inference Methods
toc.definition: Using SID to score the output of causal discovery methods against a known ground-truth DAG.
sub_questions: Why can SID change which method looks best?

toc.label: Scalability of SID
toc.definition: Empirical runtime of computing SID as the number of nodes grows.

toc.label: SID Algorithm
toc.definition: Pseudocode computing SID from two adjacency matrices via path/reachability matrices.
sub_questions: How is validity checked for all node pairs efficiently?
